instructions: Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for wrong 1-mark MCQ, 2/3 mark for wrong 2-mark MCQ.
NO negative marking for MSQ or NAT questions.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'FRUGAL'.
questions.solution: 'Frugal' means economical/sparing in use of resources. Its opposite is 'Extravagant' (spending lavishly). 'Miserly', 'Thrifty' and 'Prudent' are all synonyms or near-synonyms of frugal, not opposites.

questions.question:
Statements: All tractors are machines. Some machines are diesel-powered.
Conclusions:
I. Some tractors are diesel-powered.
II. Some diesel-powered items are machines.
Which of the following is logically valid?
questions.solution: Conclusion II is simply the logical conversion of the given statement 'Some machines are diesel-powered' → 'Some diesel-powered items are machines', which is always valid for a particular affirmative statement. Conclusion I does not necessarily follow: the diesel-powered machines need not be tractors specifically, since 'some machines' could refer entirely to non-tractor machines. Hence only II follows.

questions.question: The rainfall recorded (in mm) in a district over four consecutive months was: June = 180, July = 240, August = 210, September = 150. The percentage decrease in rainfall from July to September is closest to:
questions.solution: Percentage decrease = (July − September)/July × 100 = (240 − 150)/240 × 100 = 90/240 × 100 = 37.5%.

questions.question: A tractor consumes fuel at a constant rate. It uses 18 litres to plough 3 hectares. At the same rate, the fuel (in litres) required to plough 7.5 hectares is:
questions.solution: Fuel rate = 18/3 = 6 litres/ha. Fuel for 7.5 ha = 6 × 7.5 = 45 litres.

questions.question: A farmer sells 40% of his wheat stock and still has 300 quintals left. The original stock (in quintals) was:
questions.solution: If the original stock is x quintals, the remaining stock after selling 40% is 60% of x. So 0.6x = 300, giving x = 300/0.6 = 500 quintals.

questions.question:
Four sentences are given below. Choose the option that arranges them into a coherent paragraph.
P. This reduces evaporation losses and improves water-use efficiency in the field.
Q. Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone of the crop.
R. As a result, farmers are increasingly adopting drip systems in water-scarce regions.
S. Unlike flood irrigation, very little water is lost to runoff or deep percolation.
questions.solution: Q introduces the topic (drip irrigation delivers water to root zone). S contrasts it with flood irrigation and notes low losses. P states the consequence of low losses (reduced evaporation, better efficiency). R gives the final outcome (increasing adoption). The coherent order is Q-S-P-R.

questions.question: Six farm implements are ranked strictly by their draft requirement, from highest to lowest. The plough requires more draft than the cultivator but less than the subsoiler. The harrow requires less draft than the cultivator. The ridger requires more draft than the subsoiler but less than the leveller, which has the highest draft requirement of all. Which implement has the THIRD-highest draft requirement?
questions.solution: From the clues: Leveller > Ridger > Subsoiler > Plough > Cultivator > Harrow. Counting from the highest: 1st Leveller, 2nd Ridger, 3rd Subsoiler. Hence the subsoiler has the third-highest draft requirement.

questions.question:
A rectangular sheet of paper is folded in half along its vertical line of symmetry, bringing the right edge onto the left edge. A small triangular notch is then cut from the folded edge.
[Figure description: The rectangle (8 cm wide × 4 cm tall) is folded along the vertical centre line into a 4 cm × 4 cm folded shape. A triangular notch of base 1 cm and height 1 cm is cut with its base lying exactly on the fold line, apex pointing into the paper (away from the fold), at mid-height of the folded rectangle.]
When the paper is unfolded, the resulting hole in the original sheet is best described as:

options.A: A single triangular hole centred on the original fold line
options.B: A rhombus (diamond)-shaped hole centred on the original fold line
options.C: Two separate triangular holes, one on each half, not touching each other
options.D: A rectangular hole spanning the fold line

questions.solution: Because the notch's base lies exactly on the fold line, unfolding reflects the triangle across that line, producing a second, mirror-image triangle joined to the first along their common base (the fold line). Two triangles joined base-to-base form a rhombus (diamond) shape, centred on the original fold line at the same mid-height.

questions.question: A grain godown holds wheat and rice in the ratio 5:3 by weight, totalling 96 tonnes. If 12 tonnes of wheat is dispatched and 4 tonnes of rice is added, the new ratio of wheat to rice becomes:
questions.solution: Total parts = 5+3 = 8, so 1 part = 96/8 = 12 t. Wheat = 60 t, Rice = 36 t. After the changes: Wheat = 60 − 12 = 48 t, Rice = 36 + 4 = 40 t. New ratio = 48:40 = 6:5.

questions.question: Working alone, pump A can empty a waterlogged field in 8 hours and pump B can empty it in 12 hours. Both pumps start together, but pump A is shut down after 3 hours. In how many more hours will pump B alone empty the remaining field?
questions.solution:
Combined rate = 1/8 + 1/12 = 3/24 + 2/24 = 5/24 per hour. In 3 hours, fraction emptied = 3×5/24 = 15/24 = 5/8. Remaining fraction = 3/8. Time for B alone = (3/8) ÷ (1/12) = (3/8)×12 = 4.5 hours.
Engineering Mathematics

questions.question: The value of lim(x→0) (1 − cos 3x)/x² is:
questions.solution: Using 1 − cos(ax) ≈ a²x²/2 for small x, the limit = a²/2 with a = 3, giving 9/2 = 4.5. (Equivalently, apply L'Hôpital's rule twice: limit = 9cos(3x)/2 → 9/2 at x=0.)

questions.question: The rank of the matrix [[1,2,3],[2,4,6],[1,0,1]] is:
questions.solution: Row 2 = 2×Row 1, so Row 2 is linearly dependent on Row 1, reducing the count of independent rows. Row 3 is not a multiple of Row 1. Hence only 2 rows are linearly independent, so rank = 2.

questions.question: One of the eigenvalues of the matrix [[4,1],[0,3]] is:
questions.solution: The matrix is upper triangular, so its eigenvalues equal its diagonal entries: 4 and 3. Hence 3 is an eigenvalue.

questions.question: A fair six-faced die is rolled once. The probability of obtaining a number that is either a multiple of 3 or an even number is:
questions.solution: Multiples of 3: {3,6}. Even numbers: {2,4,6}. Union = {2,3,4,6}, which has 4 outcomes out of 6. Probability = 4/6 = 2/3.

questions.question: The mean of a set of 5 observations is 20. If one observation of value 30 is removed, the mean of the remaining 4 observations is:
questions.solution: Sum of 5 observations = 5×20 = 100. After removing 30, sum = 70. Mean of remaining 4 = 70/4 = 17.5.

questions.question: A pulley of diameter 300 mm running at 900 rpm drives a second pulley of diameter 450 mm through a belt (no slip). The speed of the driven pulley (in rpm) is:
questions.solution: For a belt drive with no slip, N₂ = N₁ × D₁/D₂ = 900 × 300/450 = 600 rpm.

questions.question: In a seed drill, the mechanism most commonly used to meter and deliver seeds at a controlled, uniform rate into the seed tube is the:
questions.solution: The fluted-roller (fluted-wheel) feed mechanism is the most widely used seed-metering device in conventional seed drills, delivering seed at a rate controlled by the exposed fluted length and roller speed.

questions.topic: Cost analysis of implements and tractors
questions.subtopic: Cost analysis of implements and tractors
questions.question: A tractor costs ₹8,00,000 with an expected useful life of 10 years and a salvage value of ₹1,00,000. Using the straight-line method, the annual depreciation (in ₹) is:
questions.solution: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost − Salvage value)/Life = (8,00,000 − 1,00,000)/10 = 7,00,000/10 = ₹70,000 per year.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a renewable source of farm power?
questions.solution: Diesel is a fossil fuel and is non-renewable. Biogas, solar PV and wind are all renewable energy sources used in agriculture.

questions.subtopic: traction theory and mechanics of tractor chassis
questions.question: The theoretical maximum tractive effort of a tractor is primarily limited by:

options.B: Weight on the driving wheels and the soil-wheel coefficient of traction

questions.solution: Maximum tractive effort = coefficient of traction × dynamic weight on the driving wheels; it is governed by the wheel-soil friction/shear limit, not merely by available engine torque.

questions.topic: Power transmission (clutch, gear box, differential, final drive, brakes)
questions.subtopic: Power transmission (clutch, gear box, differential, final drive, brakes)
questions.question: In a tractor's power transmission system, the component that allows the two rear wheels to rotate at different speeds while turning is the:
questions.solution: The differential permits the outer driving wheel to rotate faster than the inner wheel while cornering, while still transmitting equal torque, thereby preventing tyre scuffing/slip.

questions.question: Diesel has a calorific value of 45 MJ/kg and density 840 kg/m³. The energy content of 5 litres of diesel (in MJ) is:
questions.solution: Volume = 5 L = 0.005 m³. Mass = density × volume = 840 × 0.005 = 4.2 kg. Energy = mass × calorific value = 4.2 × 45 = 189 MJ.

questions.question: The time taken by runoff to travel from the remotest (hydraulically most distant) point of a watershed to its outlet is called:
questions.solution: Time of concentration is defined as the time for runoff to travel from the hydraulically most remote point of the watershed to the outlet.

questions.question: The soil water content at which a soil changes from a plastic to a liquid state is termed the:
questions.solution: The liquid limit (one of the Atterberg limits) is the water content at the boundary between the plastic and liquid states of a fine-grained soil.

questions.question: The ratio of the volume of voids to the total volume of a soil mass is termed:
questions.solution: Porosity n = Vv/V(total). (Void ratio, by contrast, is defined as Vv/Vs, the ratio of void volume to solids volume.)

questions.question: In a levelling survey, the difference between the back sight (BS) and fore sight (FS) readings taken from the same instrument station gives the:

options.B: Difference in elevation between the two staff points

questions.solution: Rise or fall between two consecutive staff points = BS − FS (a positive value indicates a rise, negative indicates a fall), directly giving the difference in elevation between the two points.

questions.question: The primary purpose of providing sub-surface field drains in agricultural land is to:

options.B: Lower the water table and remove excess soil water

questions.solution: Sub-surface drains remove excess gravitational water from the root zone, lowering the water table and improving aeration/trafficability, which is their primary purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following are commonly used methods of agricultural land drainage?
questions.solution: Open ditch drains, subsurface pipe (tile) drains, and mole drains are all established methods of removing excess water from agricultural land. 'Sprinkler drains' does not exist as a drainage method — sprinklers are an irrigation (water application) method, not a drainage technique, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: The drying period during which the moisture removal rate remains constant with time (free surface moisture evaporating unimpeded) is called the:
questions.solution: During the constant rate period, drying rate depends only on external conditions (air temperature, humidity, velocity) as free surface moisture evaporates unimpeded, giving a constant moisture removal rate with time.

questions.question: Which law of size reduction states that the energy required is proportional to the new surface area created?
questions.solution: Rittinger's Law states that energy input is proportional to the new surface area created during size reduction, i.e., E ∝ (1/Dp2 − 1/Dp1).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding size-reduction equipment are correct?

options.A: Hammer mills operate primarily on the principle of impact
options.B: Roller mills operate primarily on the principle of compression/shear
options.C: Ball mills are typically used for fine grinding using attrition and impact

questions.solution: Hammer mills use impact of rotating hammers, roller mills use compression/shear between rollers, and ball mills achieve fine grinding through attrition and impact of grinding media — all correct. Belt conveyors are material-HANDLING equipment, not size-reduction equipment, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: Grain is stored in a cylindrical bin of diameter 4 m and height 6 m. Taking the bulk density of the grain as 750 kg/m³, and assuming the bin is filled to 80% of its volume, find the mass of grain stored (in tonnes), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution: Bin volume = πr²h = π × 2² × 6 = 75.40 m³. Filled volume = 0.80 × 75.40 = 60.32 m³. Mass = 60.32 × 750 = 45,239 kg = 45.24 tonnes.

questions.question: A lot of wheat weighing 2000 kg is at 16% moisture content (wet basis) and is to be dried to 13% moisture content (wet basis) for safe storage. Find the mass of water to be removed (in kg), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution: Dry matter (unchanged by drying) = W₁(1−M₁) = 2000 × 0.84 = 1680 kg. Final total mass W₂ = Dry matter/(1−M₂) = 1680/0.87 = 1931.03 kg. Water removed = W₁ − W₂ = 2000 − 1931.03 = 68.97 kg.

questions.question: Pasteurization of milk is primarily intended to:

options.A: Sterilize the milk completely, destroying all micro-organisms and spores
options.B: Destroy pathogenic micro-organisms while retaining most nutritional and sensory qualities
options.C: Increase the fat content of milk
options.D: Remove water from milk to concentrate it

questions.solution: Pasteurization uses a controlled heat treatment to destroy pathogenic (disease-causing) micro-organisms and most spoilage organisms while retaining the milk's nutritional value and sensory qualities; it is not intended to achieve complete sterilization.

questions.question: Which of the following are recognized methods of food preservation?
questions.solution: Canning, freezing, and irradiation are all established food-preservation methods that inhibit microbial growth/spoilage. Homogenization is a mechanical process that reduces and disperses fat globules to prevent creaming; it is not a preservation method, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: For f(x,y) = x²y + 3xy², the value of ∂²f/∂x∂y at the point (1, 2) is:
questions.solution: ∂f/∂x = 2xy + 3y². Differentiating with respect to y: ∂²f/∂x∂y = 2x + 6y. At (1,2): 2(1) + 6(2) = 2 + 12 = 14.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral I = ∫₀² (3x² + 2x) dx, and then compute √I. Give the answer rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution: I = [x³ + x²]₀² = (8+4) − 0 = 12. √I = √12 = 3.464 ≈ 3.46, which lies in the range 3.40 to 3.50.

questions.question: The matrix A = [[5,2],[2,2]] has eigenvalues λ₁ and λ₂ with λ₁ > λ₂. Find the value of (λ₁ − λ₂)².
questions.solution: Trace = 7, Determinant = (5×2) − (2×2) = 10 − 4 = 6. Characteristic equation: λ² − 7λ + 6 = 0 → (λ−1)(λ−6) = 0 → λ = 6, 1. λ₁ − λ₂ = 6 − 1 = 5. (λ₁−λ₂)² = 25.

questions.question:
Solve dy/dx + 2y = 0 with y(0) = 5. Find y at x = ln 2 (natural log), rounded to two decimal places.
Farm Machinery (from Q.16)
questions.solution:
General solution: y = Ce^(−2x). Using y(0)=5, C=5, so y = 5e^(−2x). At x = ln2: e^(−2ln2) = e^(ln(1/4)) = 1/4. y = 5 × 0.25 = 1.25.
Farm Machinery

questions.subtopic: soil tillage & forces on a tillage tool
questions.question: A tillage tool operates at a depth of 200 mm and width of 300 mm in soil with a specific resistance of 60 kN/m². The draft force required (in kN) is:
questions.solution: Draft = specific resistance × cross-sectional area = 60 kN/m² × (0.2 m × 0.3 m) = 60 × 0.06 = 3.6 kN.

questions.subtopic: soil tillage & forces on a tillage tool
questions.question: A tractor pulls a mouldboard plough requiring a draft of 12 kN at a forward speed of 4 km/h. If the drawbar (transmission) efficiency of the tractor is 80%, find the engine power required (in kW), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution: Speed = 4 km/h = 4000/3600 = 1.111 m/s. Drawbar power = Draft × speed = 12 × 1.111 = 13.33 kW. Engine power = Drawbar power / efficiency = 13.33/0.80 = 16.67 kW.

questions.question: A chain drive has a driving sprocket with 20 teeth rotating at 300 rpm and a driven sprocket with 45 teeth. The speed of the driven sprocket (in rpm), rounded to two decimal places, is:
questions.solution: For a chain drive, N₂ = N₁ × T₁/T₂ = 300 × 20/45 = 133.33 rpm.

questions.question:
A boom sprayer travels at 1.5 m/s and delivers a total discharge of 12 litres per minute (lpm) through a boom of swath width 8 m. Find the application rate (in litres per hectare), rounded to the nearest whole number.
Farm Power (from Q.19)
questions.solution:
Area covered per minute = swath width × distance travelled per minute = 8 m × (1.5×60 m) = 8 × 90 = 720 m²/min. Application rate = Discharge/Area = 12 L / 720 m² = 0.01667 L/m². Converting to per hectare (1 ha = 10,000 m²): 0.01667 × 10,000 = 166.7 L/ha.
Farm Power

questions.question: A biogas plant produces biogas with a methane content of 60% (by volume) and the calorific value of pure methane is 35 MJ/m³. If the plant produces 8 m³ of biogas per day, find the total energy available per day (in MJ), assuming only the methane fraction contributes to the calorific value.
questions.solution: Volume of methane = 8 × 0.60 = 4.8 m³/day. Energy available = 4.8 × 35 = 168 MJ/day.

questions.subtopic: traction theory and mechanics of tractor chassis
questions.question: A tractor weighing 18 kN has 70% of its weight on the rear (driving) wheels. The coefficient of traction between tyre and soil is 0.5, and the motion resistance of the tractor is 1.8 kN. Find the maximum drawbar pull available (in kN).
questions.solution: Weight on driving wheels = 0.70 × 18 = 12.6 kN. Maximum tractive effort = 0.5 × 12.6 = 6.3 kN. Drawbar pull = Tractive effort − Motion resistance = 6.3 − 1.8 = 4.5 kN.

questions.question: A four-stroke single-cylinder diesel engine has a bore of 100 mm and a stroke of 120 mm. The swept volume (in cm³), rounded to the nearest whole number, is:
An air-standard Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 8. Taking γ = 1.4, the theoretical thermal efficiency of the cycle (in %) is:

A worker's resting heart rate is 70 beats/min. During a field operation, the average working heart rate is 130 beats/min, and the worker's maximum sustainable heart rate is 190 beats/min. Find the percentage of Heart Rate Reserve (%HRR) utilized during the operation, using %HRR = (HR(work) − HR(rest))/(HR(max) − HR(rest)) × 100.
Soil & Water Conservation Engineering (from Q.23)
questions.solution:
%HRR = (130 − 70)/(190 − 70) × 100 = 60/120 × 100 = 50%.
Soil & Water Conservation Engineering

questions.question: A watershed of area 250 hectares receives a rainfall of 60 mm in a storm. If the runoff coefficient is 0.35, find the volume of surface runoff generated (in m³).
questions.solution: Area = 250 ha = 2,500,000 m². Rainfall depth = 0.06 m. Volume of rainfall = 2,500,000 × 0.06 = 150,000 m³. Runoff volume = 0.35 × 150,000 = 52,500 m³.

questions.question: For a small watershed of area 40 hectares, the rainfall intensity is 50 mm/h and the runoff coefficient is 0.4. Using the Rational Formula Q = CiA/360 (Q in m³/s, i in mm/h, A in hectares), find the peak discharge (in m³/s), rounded to two decimal places.

Water flows through a pipe of diameter 150 mm with a velocity of 2 m/s. It then enters a second pipe of diameter 100 mm. Using the continuity equation, find the velocity of flow (in m/s) in the second pipe.
questions.solution: By continuity, A₁V₁ = A₂V₂, so V₂ = V₁(D₁/D₂)² = 2 × (150/100)² = 2 × 2.25 = 4.5 m/s.

questions.question: Water flows through a venturimeter with inlet diameter 200 mm and throat diameter 100 mm. The difference in piezometric head between inlet and throat is 0.5 m. Taking g = 9.81 m/s² and neglecting losses, find the velocity of flow at the throat (in m/s), rounded to two decimal places, using continuity (A₁V₁ = A₂V₂) together with Bernoulli's equation between the inlet and throat.
questions.solution: Area ratio gives V₁ = V₂/(D₁/D₂)² = V₂/4 (since (200/100)²=4). Bernoulli: (V₂² − V₁²)/2g = h = 0.5. Substituting V₁ = V₂/4: V₂²(1 − 1/16)/2g = 0.5 → V₂² × (15/16) = 2×9.81×0.5 = 9.81 → V₂² = 9.81×16/15 = 10.464 → V₂ = 3.235 m/s.

questions.question: Using the Universal Soil Loss Equation A = R·K·LS·C·P, estimate the annual soil loss (in t/ha/yr) for a field with R = 400 MJ·mm/(ha·h·yr), K = 0.30 t·ha·h/(ha·MJ·mm), LS = 1.5, C = 0.25, and P = 0.8.

A watershed has a gross soil erosion rate of 40 t/ha/yr over an area of 500 ha. If the sediment delivery ratio is 0.3, find the total sediment yield delivered to the watershed outlet per year (in tonnes).
Irrigation & Drainage Engineering (from Q.27)
questions.solution:
Total gross erosion = 40 × 500 = 20,000 t/yr. Sediment yield = Delivery ratio × Gross erosion = 0.3 × 20,000 = 6,000 t/yr.
Irrigation & Drainage Engineering

questions.question: A confined aquifer has a transmissivity of 500 m²/day. If the hydraulic gradient is 0.002, find the discharge per unit width of the aquifer (in m³/day per metre width), using Darcy's law q = T·i.
questions.solution: q = T × i = 500 × 0.002 = 1.0 m³/day per metre width.

questions.question: A soil has a field capacity of 28% and a permanent wilting point of 12% (both on a weight basis). The bulk density of the soil is 1.4 g/cm³. Find the total available water in the top 0.6 m of soil depth (in mm).
questions.solution: Available water fraction (by weight) = 28% − 12% = 16% = 0.16. Depth of available water = (FC−PWP)/100 × Bulk density × Soil depth = 0.16 × 1.4 × 600 mm = 134.4 mm.

questions.topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.subtopic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.question: An irrigation channel must carry a discharge of 2 m³/s. Using Manning's equation Q = (1/n)·A·R^(2/3)·S^(1/2) with n = 0.025 and bed slope S = 0.0004, and given that for this channel's rectangular cross-section (bed width = 4 × depth) at the design condition the flow area is A = 4y² and the hydraulic radius is R = 0.8y (both given, so no iteration is needed), find the normal flow depth y (in m), rounded to two decimal places.

A tube well fully penetrates a confined aquifer of thickness 15 m and hydraulic conductivity 20 m/day. When pumped at a steady rate, the drawdown at the well is 3 m, and at an observation well 50 m away it is 0.8 m. Using the Thiem equation Q = 2πKb(s₁−s₂)/ln(r₂/r₁), with well radius r₁ = 0.15 m and r₂ = 50 m, find the discharge Q (in m³/day).
Agricultural Process Engineering (from Q.29)
Paddy weighing 1000 kg at 22% moisture content (wet basis) is to be dried to 12% moisture content (wet basis). Find the mass of water removed (in kg), rounded to two decimal places.

A single-effect evaporator concentrating milk evaporates 500 kg/h of water. The steam economy of the evaporator (kg of water evaporated per kg of steam supplied) is 0.9. Find the steam consumption (in kg/h), rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.solution: Steam consumption = Water evaporated/Steam economy = 500/0.9 = 555.6 kg/h.

questions.question: A material is crushed such that its average particle diameter is reduced from 20 mm to 5 mm, consuming 12 kJ/kg of energy. Using Rittinger's Law E = K_R(1/Dp2 − 1/Dp1), find the additional energy (in kJ/kg) required to further reduce the same material from 5 mm to 2 mm, rounded to two decimal places.

A grain kernel has axial dimensions: length 8 mm, width 4 mm, and thickness 3 mm. Find its geometric mean diameter Dg = (L·W·T)^(1/3), in mm, rounded to two decimal places.
Dairy & Food Engineering (from Q.34)
questions.solution:
Dg = (8 × 4 × 3)^(1/3) = (96)^(1/3) = 4.58 mm.
Dairy & Food Engineering

questions.question: For steady-state, one-dimensional heat conduction through a composite plane wall made of two layers in series, which of the following statements are correct?

options.A: The heat flux is the same through both layers
options.B: The overall thermal resistance is the sum of the individual layer resistances
options.C: The temperature gradient is steeper in the layer with higher thermal conductivity
options.D: The total temperature drop across the wall is independent of the individual layer conductivities

questions.solution: In steady-state series conduction, the same heat flux passes through both layers (A is correct), and thermal resistances in series add (R_total = R1+R2, B is correct). Since q = −k(dT/dx) and q is constant, a LOWER conductivity requires a STEEPER gradient for the same flux, not a higher conductivity — so C is false. The total temperature drop for a given heat flux depends directly on the total resistance, which depends on both layers' conductivities — so D is false.

questions.question: Milk flowing through a plate heat exchanger is heated from 5°C to 72°C. The mass flow rate of milk is 2000 kg/h and its specific heat is 3.9 kJ/(kg·°C). Find the heat duty required (in kW), rounded to one decimal place.

The decimal reduction time (D-value) of a bacterial spore at 121°C is 2.5 minutes. If the initial spore load is 10⁶ per can, find the heating time (in minutes) required at 121°C to reduce the spore load to 10¹ per can, using log₁₀(N₀/N) = t/D.
questions.solution:
log₁₀(N₀/N) = log₁₀(10⁶/10¹) = log₁₀(10⁵) = 5. Heating time t = D × 5 = 2.5 × 5 = 12.5 minutes.
